$comment: Where things live inside a host pack, asserted from both sides.
`scripts/build_local_host_pack.py` writes this layout and
`desktop/locald/src/native_host_pack.rs` reads it. Neither had any idea
what the other did. The producer's only tests assert `npm_executable`;
the consumer hard-codes a dozen paths and, when one is missing, fails at
the point a user is watching a progress bar -- with `NotFound` and the
name of a file they have never heard of.
The two are also built by different jobs on different triggers. A release
run produces the pack; a PR runs the consumer's unit tests against a
fixture the same PR wrote. So a rename lands green on both sides and is
discovered by whoever installs the release.
The rule this file exists to serve, from docs/testing.md: a stub is
legitimate only when a contract test pins both sides against one
committed artifact. This is that artifact for the host pack.
`required` names things the consumer refuses to start without, and lists
the alternatives it accepts in the order it tries them. Order matters:
Next's standalone output nests the server under a directory named after
the workspace, and which name that is has changed with Next versions --
so the consumer tries all three and the producer resolves the same three.
`derived` names paths the consumer builds by joining rather than probing.
There is no fallback for these: they either exist or the service that
needs them starts and then fails at runtime, which is worse than failing
here.
`producer_writes` is the literal the *producer* must contain for that
entry, which is not always the path -- the script assembles some of these
from pieces. Where it is null the producer is checked by running it
instead, which is stronger. Both lists use it.
`must_not_be_empty` exists because presence is the one thing that is never
the problem. A zero-byte `lemma-client.js`, an empty `migrations/` or a
truncated `alembic.ini` all pass an existence check and all produce an
install that gets further before it fails. Directories are checked for
having an entry; files for having a byte.
`named_by_consumer` is false for a path the consumer needs but never
spells: `lemma_apps_config.json` is read by `import_connector_catalog.py`,
which locald runs. It still has to be in the pack -- without it the
connector setup fails -- but the Rust half cannot look for it in a file
that does not mention it.
